front.title: Latency Guarantee with Stateless Fair Queuing

abstract.t: This document specifies the implementation of the stateless fair queuing framework defined in Recommendations ITU-T Y.3129 [Y.3129] and Y.3148 [Y.3148]. The framework provides end-to-end (E2E) latency bounds to flows without requiring core nodes to maintain per-flow state. For each packet, the entrance node of a flow computes the ideal service completion time under a fluid model, referred to as the Finish Time (FT), and encodes it in the packet header. Each subsequent core node updates the FT by adding a delay factor that is determined by the flow and the nodes. Schedulers serve queued packets in ascending order of FT. This mechanism provides strong isolation among flows. The E2E latency bound of a flow depends on the flow's own parameters, such as its maximum burst size and service rate, and on link parameters, such as the link capacity and the maximum packet length among the flows sharing the link. This document specifies the required metadata and its encoding formats, the admission control procedure, and an approximation of stateless fair queuing using a strict priority (SP) scheduler.
